'''Marianne Baudler''' (27 April 1921 – 5 March 2003) was a German chemist.<ref name=":0" /> She is known for her research on [[phosphorus]].<ref>{{cite book |date=2010 |last=Lai Yoong |first=Goon |title=Follow the chemistry : lure, lore, and life : an autobiography of Goh Lai Yoong  |publisher=World Scientific |location=Singapore |page=142 |ISBN=9789814304009 }}</ref>

==Life==
Marianne Baudler was born in Stettin.<ref name=":0" /> She started studying Chemistry at the [[Technische Hochschule Dresden]] in April 1940 and finished her studies with a Diplom in 1943.<ref name=":0" /> From 1943 to 1946, she worked on her dissertation in the group of [[Franz Fehér]] at the [[University of Göttingen]].<ref name=":0" /> Starting in 1949, Baudler performed research at the [[University of Cologne]]. In 1952, she finished her habilitation.<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Baudler|first=Marianne|title=Untersuchungen über Di-Phosphorsäuren: Gleichz. e. Beitr. zur Kenntnis d. Phosphor-Phosphor-Bindg|date=1959|degree=Habilitation|url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=idn%3D481165363|place=Köln}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> In 1963 she became extraordinary professor at the [[University of Cologne]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1968, the full professorship followed. From 1986 on, she was an emeritus professor.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Her research focused on:

* Small-ring phosphorus compounds<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|date=1986|title=Wer ist's?: Marianne Baudler|journal=Nachrichten aus Chemie, Technik und Laboratorium|language=en|volume=34|issue=7|pages=668–669|doi=10.1002/nadc.19860340714|issn=1868-0054}}</ref>
* Phosphorus hydrides<ref name=":1" />
* Polycyclic organophosphanes<ref name=":1" />
* Mono- and polycyclic compounds of arsenic<ref name=":1" />
